prerequisites: Knowledge of linear algebra and infinitesimal calculus acquired in Algebra and Calculus courses.

learning_outcomes.text: Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that starts from the base of general secondary education, and is usually found at a level that, although supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that involve knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competences that are usually demonstrated by elaborating and defending arguments and solving problems within their field of study.

Ability to solve mathematical problems that may arise in engineering. Aptitude to apply knowledge on: linear algebra; geometry; differential geometry; differential and integral calculus; differential and partial differential equations; numerical methods; numerical algorithms, statistics and optimization.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to manage specifications, regulations and mandatory standards.

syllabus_topics: General concepts. Differential equation of a family of plane curves.
The first-order equation. General solution and particular solution.
Existence and uniqueness theorem for solutions.
Graphical representation of solutions. Isoclines. Direction field.
Separable variables equations. Homogeneous equations.
Exact differential equations. Integrating factor.
The linear equation. General solution.
Bernoulli's and Riccati's equations.
Equations not solved for the derivative. Lagrange. Clairaut.
Singular solutions.
Geometric applications. Orthogonal trajectories.
Definitions. The Cauchy problem. Existence and uniqueness theorem for solutions.
Elementary integration methods.
The linear equation. The linear differential operator.
Fundamental theory of linear equations. Fundamental system of solutions. Wronskian.
Reduction of order of the homogeneous linear equation knowing a solution.
Homogeneous linear equations with constant coefficients.
Non-homogeneous linear equations. General integral. Method of variation of parameters.
Other ways of finding solutions: Method of undetermined coefficients. Operational method.
Euler's and Legendre's equations.
Definition. Existence conditions.
Transforms of some elementary functions. Properties of the Laplace transform.
The inverse transform.
Convolution of functions. Convolution theorem.
Application of the Laplace transform to the solution of differential equations.
Solutions of nth order differential equations using power series. Method description.
Solutions near an ordinary point.
Regular singular points. Frobenius method. Particular cases.
Bessel's equation.
Generation of systems. Congruence of curves.
First-order systems.
Some general solution methods. Elimination. Integrable combinations. D operator.
Linear systems.
Homogeneous linear systems. Solution structure.
Homogeneous linear systems with constant coefficients.
Non-homogeneous systems.
Analyze the behavior of solutions of an autonomous system.
General concepts: Phase plane. Trajectory. Critical points.
Definition and concept of system stability. Linear systems. Simple types of equilibrium points.
Non-linear systems.
Hurwitz criterion.
Basic concepts of partial differential equations (PDEs): Order of an equation. Particular solution. General solution.
Boundary conditions: Dirichlet. Neumann. Robin.
Equations of interest in mathematical physics: Wave equation. Heat equation. Laplace equation.
Second-order linear PDEs. Types of equations.
Euler's equation. General solution.
The Method of Separation of Variables.
teaching_methods: Interaction with the teaching team, tutor teachers and students
assessment_rules: The final grade is the maximum of the exam grade or (0.9 * exam grade) + (0.1 * continuous assessment grade), provided the exam grade is 5 or higher. If the exam grade is less than 5, the continuous assessment grade does not count. A minimum of 5 points in the in-person exam is required to pass the course. The continuous assessment grade is valid for both ordinary and extraordinary calls.
